issues.legal_issue: A conviction for culpable homicide not amounting to murder cannot stand when the alleged victim survives and no death is caused.
material_facts: The appellant was convicted by the High Court of culpable homicide not amounting to murder for striking the victim with the back of a cutting tool.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not convict the appellant of culpable homicide not amounting to murder because no death had been caused.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 299, 300 and 304 of the Indian Penal Code establish that culpable homicide and its punishment under section 304 require a death to have been caused. Section 304 distinguishes between cases involving guilty intention and those involving guilty knowledge; no earlier cases are cited.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_culpable_homicide_c: A person appeals a conviction for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
predicates.no_death_caused: The person allegedly harmed survives and no death is caused by the accused.
predicates.culpable_homicide_conviction_cannot_stan: The conviction for culpable homicide not amounting to murder cannot stand.

issues.definition: When a person appeals a culpable-homicide conviction and no death was caused, that conviction cannot stand.

issues.legal_issue: An accused is entitled to acquittal where the prosecution has suppressed the true occurrence, the accused sustained injuries in that occurrence, and the right of private defence is available.
material_facts: The dispute concerned the harvesting of crops from land over which both sides claimed title and possession.
The appellant and another accused sustained injuries in the same occurrence as the informant and his brother.
The appellant said that he was injured while warding off a spear blow aimed at his chest.

The High Court found that the prosecution had suppressed the manner of occurrence and had not given its true version, and that the right of private defence of person and property could not be ruled out.
issues.conclusion: Given the finding that the prosecution had not disclosed the true occurrence and that the right of private defence was available, the appellant was entitled to be acquitted.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 101 and 104 of the Indian Penal Code concern the right of private defence. The court applied that right in light of the finding that the prosecution had suppressed the true occurrence and that the accused's account of the incident could not be ruled out; no earlier cases are cited.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: A person appeals a criminal conviction arising from an alleged assault.

predicates.prosecution_suppressed_true_occurrence: The prosecution did not disclose the true manner of the occurrence.

predicates.accused_entitled_to_acquittal: The accused is entitled to acquittal.

issues.definition: When a person appeals a criminal conviction, was injured in the same occurrence, and the prosecution suppressed the true occurrence while private defence was available, the person is entitled to acquittal.
